decisions.reason: Footnote 3's "respiratory rate > 30" feeds the shock-likely rule, so the questions that rule needs should be asked when it is present.
"pulse ≥ 100" is one of the Circulation column's conditions for acting, like SBP < 80, which both builds use as a trigger.

decisions.difference: A: Dyspnea  vs  B: Difficulty breathing (A narrower)
decisions.reason: The page says "difficulty breathing"; B's concept is the page's word, and Dyspnea is a descendant of it.

decisions.difference: A: Acute heart failure (disorder)  vs  B: its footnote features
decisions.final_expr: Acute heart failure, Swelling of lower limb, Orthopnea, Dyspnea on exertion
decisions.reason: The page names "acute heart failure³", and footnote 3 spells out leg swelling and difficulty breathing that worsens on lying down or with effort, so the concept and its features are all asked.

decisions.difference: A: Clouded consciousness  vs  B: Acute confusion (B narrower)
decisions.reason: "confusion" has no SNOMED term of its own; the app records it both as AVPU "Confused" (Clouded consciousness) and as the warning sign "Confusion" (Acute confusion).

decisions.difference: A: Glasgow coma scale, 3 … 8  vs  B: (none; GCS judged not representable)
decisions.reason: The page says "If GCS ≤ 8" in the red box; these six existing findings express it exactly, at the cost of firing only if a GCS total is recorded as one of them.
The "Gasping or not breathing" branch means agonal gasping in an unresponsive patient, alongside Gasping for breath.

decisions.difference: A: (none)  vs  B: Swelling of lower limb, Orthopnea, Dyspnea on exertion
decisions.reason: Footnote 3 (first) lists exactly these features of acute heart failure; they are needed as evidence in the pulse < 50 instability criterion.

decisions.difference: A: Acute heart failure (disorder)  vs  B: (or Swelling of lower limb, Orthopnea, Dyspnea on exertion)
decisions.final_expr: (or (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Acute heart failure" "disorder")) (and (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Swelling of lower limb" "finding")) (or (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Orthopnea" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Dyspnea on exertion" "finding")))))
decisions.reason: The page names acute heart failure, and footnote 3 describes it as leg swelling with breathlessness that worsens lying down or with effort, one picture rather than three alternatives; B's any-of reading would count leg swelling alone.

decisions.difference: A: Glasgow coma scale, 3 … 8  vs  B: (none)
decisions.reason: The red box says "If GCS ≤ 8, intubate patient", one of the ABC/consciousness compromises the priority rule gathers.

decisions.difference: A: (none)  vs  B: an entry gate (and <Unresponsive, Cardiac arrest, Respiratory obstruction, Difficulty breathing, SpO2 < 94, RR < 9, SBP < 80, pulse < 50> (or …))
decisions.reason: The page doesn't define "the emergency patient". Almost every gate item also appears in the inner or, so the gate repeated the trigger without restricting anything; A's ungated form is kept.
It belongs to "Gasping or not breathing" in the first priority rule.

decisions.difference: A: (none; difficulty breathing alone deliberately excluded)  vs  B: Difficulty breathing
decisions.reason: The page puts "If difficulty breathing or oxygen saturation < 94%" in one sentence, and both builds already include SpO2 < 94; leaving out its partner would be a clinical judgment the page doesn't make. It makes any difficulty breathing an Emergency.

decisions.difference: A: Clouded consciousness  vs  B: Acute confusion (shock likely)
decisions.reason: "confusion/restlessness": both recorded forms of confusion are or-ed with restlessness.

decisions.difference: Structure of shock likely: A: (and SBP < 80, pulse ≥ 100, RR > 30, confusion/restlessness, weakness)  vs  B: (or …)
decisions.final_expr: (and (< SBP 80) (>= pulse 100) (> RR 30) (or Clouded consciousness, Acute confusion, Restlessness) Asthenia)
decisions.reason: The footnote lists signs with no "or" (unlike the "chest pain or acute heart failure" list) ending in "shock likely", the same shape as the tension pneumothorax list both builders read as all-of. B's any-of reading makes pulse ≥ 100 alone probable shock.

decisions.difference: Structure: A: two Emergency rules  vs  B: one
decisions.final_expr: Emergency: emergency patient unresponsive, pulseless or not breathing; Emergency: emergency patient with airway, breathing, circulation or consciousness compromise
decisions.reason: The page has the flowchart's top branches (no response, no pulse, gasping) and the ABC columns as two distinct stages; the split follows them and keeps each rule's description specific.

notes: Both builds passed. A was the base for its structure (two ungated priority rules, GCS 3–8, all-of shock). B contributed the page's own term Difficulty breathing (trigger and priority), Agonal respiration, Acute confusion, and the acute heart failure footnote features. In the priority rule those features are combined as leg swelling AND (orthopnoea OR dyspnoea on exertion), alongside the Acute heart failure concept. The last two decisions are structural and are not separate rows in diff.json. B's entry gate was dropped. The two builds' remaining questions are merged, and the flowchart is A's, updated.
